title: C# _Set hook is ignored during Assembly Reload for virtual properties, breaking Custom Source Generators and Dynamic Scenarios
body:
### Tested versions

4.6.dev3

### System information

Godot v4.6.dev3.mono - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8180) - AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 63.65 GiB memory

### Issue description

In Godot C#, standard fields marked with [Export] work correctly during Hot Reload because Godot's built-in Source Generators run at compile time to generate the necessary glue code for serialization and property registration.

However, for advanced scenarios—such as Custom Source Generators or dynamic tools—we often cannot rely on Godot's built-in SG (e.g., when properties are generated dynamically or exist only as virtual proxies). In these cases, we rely on the GodotObject virtual hooks: _GetPropertyList, _Get, and _Set.

The Problem: While _Set works perfectly for serialization (saving/loading .tscn/.tres) and Editor interaction, it is completely bypassed during C# Assembly Reload (Hot Reload).

It appears the reload mechanism relies on reflection or the pre-generated glue code to restore state, ignoring the _Set hook for properties that do not have a direct C# field counterpart.

Why this is critical: This effectively breaks the ability to create robust Custom Source Generators or advanced tooling in C#. If a developer generates properties virtually (backed by Dictionary, Variant, or Metadata) to avoid boilerplate or implement custom serialization logic, the data is inevitably lost every time the user modifies a script, rendering the tool unstable for production use.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a C# script with [Tool].

2. Override _GetPropertyList to expose a virtual property (e.g., "VirtualInt").

3. Override _Set to store the value in a private field (e.g., _backingField). Add a GD.Print log inside _Set to track calls.

4. Override _Get to return _backingField.

5. Attach the script to a Node in the scene.

6. Change the value of "VirtualInt" in the Inspector. Note that _Set is called (log printed).

7. Modify the C# script (e.g., add a comment) and build the project to trigger a Hot Reload.

8. Observed: _Set is NOT called during the reload process. The value in the Inspector resets to the default (0).

9. Expected: _Set should be called with the cached value to restore the object's state after the assembly reload.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[set-not-called.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23972061/set-not-called.zip)
